testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: rebase-check job (pull_request-only branch-currency assertion, not meaningful in a worktree of origin/main); proc-macos job (node --test tests/proc.test.mjs on macOS) (subsumed by the full suite on this macOS host); smoke-omp job (needs pinned omp installed via bun, absent here); install-and-smoke job (needs pinned omp installed via bun and network, absent here).

survived.claim: After this PR, no row in board-server.test.mjs or cockpit-tick-nonblocking.test.mjs checks that the real answers() probe reads a refused connect as free. A regression that makes answers() read every port as held passes the whole of both files, but before the PR it failed 4 rows.
survived.evidence: In the copy, mutated tests/support/cockpit-port.mjs from `socket.once("error", (e) => done(e.code !== "ECONNREFUSED"))` to `done(true)`, then ran `node --test --test-reporter=spec tests/board-server.test.mjs tests/cockpit-tick-nonblocking.test.mjs` → 'ℹ tests 69 / pass 69 / fail 0 / skipped 0'. Then applied `git apply -R pr.diff` (the pre-PR tree) with the same mutant and ran the watchWindow|heldWindowExit rows → 'fail 4': 'with nothing held', 'landing past a candidate nothing held', 'allHeld()' and 'heldWindowExit' each ✖. All 4 rows now use scriptedWatch, so the default probe's free-reading has no test. If answers() regressed this way, blockerBefore() in the derived-port CLI rows would excuse every landing past ports[0], and a real scan bug would surface as a heldOutside skip, not a failure.
survived.suggested_fix: Add one real-socket row that pins answers()'s refusal-means-free reading, using the brief's second approach: draw a port with unheldPorts(1) and run watchWindow([port]) with no probe. If allHeld() is true, try to listen on the port: EADDRINUSE means an outside holder, so t.skip(heldOutside(port)); otherwise assert allHeld() is false. This keeps the default path covered without bringing back the cross-process flake.

Reproduced in my own copy of the snapshot. I changed the answers() probe in tests/support/cockpit-port.mjs to `done(true)`, so every port reads as held. Running both files then gave exit 0, tests 69, pass 69, fail 0, cancelled 0, skipped 0. The only real-probe row, board-server.test.mjs:843 (a held-then-released candidate), still passes under the mutant. Both of its candidates read as held, so blockerBefore(landed) returns the first one, which is the asserted value. The four rows that used to catch this mutant (nothing held, landing past a candidate nothing held, allHeld, heldWindowExit) now use scriptedWatch. I did not rerun the pre-PR tree, so the 'failed 4 rows before' half rests on the finder's evidence. The claim that the real probe's free-reading is unchecked holds. The same-name `done(true)` grep matched 3 lines, so the sed may have hit other lines too, but the mutant ran and the suite stayed green. red: n/a (no failing test under the mutant); mutant run: node --test tests/board-server.test.mjs tests/cockpit-tick-nonblocking.test.mjs → exit 0, 69 pass.
